properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-08-20 to Minard Run Oil Co in Jenks Twp, Forest county. 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Minard Run Oil Co
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-08-20
Violation Code: 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID: 859453
Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-20
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed through a culvert under the access road and continued to spread out and flow through vegetation approximately 400 feet. Moody & Associates has been employed to coordinate the clean-up of this crude oil release. Jordan Sipos, P.G. completed the testing to establish the extent of the release and contaminated soil. Clean-up of the contaminated soil appears to be completed. Soil removal has been extended several hundred feet north of the area originally flagged as showing oil contamination from the release. Four piles of contaminated soil have been secured adjacent to the clean-up area until testing has been completed for disposal. A temporary road has been stoned to access the area and for the eventual removal of the contaminated soil. Manifest for the removal and disposal of the contaminated soil need to be submitted to the Department to lift the violations associated with this release. The removal of the contaminated soil was completed with the least disturbance possible to the surrounding vegetation and without creating a muddy unstable area. Replacement of topsoil and vegetation of this area needs to be coordinated with landowner and State Forest representatives. 15 Day initial Response Letter received July 1, 2019 for Alternate Remediation provision found in the PA DEP Oil and Gas Spill Policy. The report for the clean-up and restoration of the area needs to be submitted to the Department and approved before violations can be lifted.

CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: William H Brawand
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-10-04
Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 864247
Permit API: 047-24421
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-10-04
Comments: This inspection was performed following the Department receiving a complaint of possible brine dumping in a ditch line near the Brawand 53 well location. This inspection was performed with WQSS Rich Sheriff. The well is equipped with an electric powered pumpjack, and appears to be producing. The stuffing box seems to have leaked at times, as there is a coating of oil on the wellhead and ground. The well is tagged and the access road and site are stable. There is a ditch line/UNT to Johnson Run that flows near the entrance to this site. The ditch flows to the southeast and into a small pond approximately 500 feet away, which has an outlet to continue down-gradient. A check with a handheld conductivity meter and probe shows elevated levels in this channel immediately around a culvert and at various spots flowing downstream. There is also evidence of tree and other vegetative death along the immediate banks of this UNT, indicating that brine was likely discharged into this channel. (See attached photos) The Operator may contact WQSS Rich Sheriff at 814-723-0973 to discuss this incident.

Permit API: 065-26370
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-04-02
Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Spring Creek Road in July 2008. A spill was reported to the Department at 16:28 on April 1, 2019. The spill occurred when the brine tank overflowed. Oil was allowed to escape and contact the ground surface, but no evidence of a brine discharge could be seen. The reported release amount was of approximately 30 gallons, and conditions at the site at the time of inspection indicate that this estimate is reasonable. Because the estimated spill volume was less than 1 bbl, a visual clean-up at this site is appropriate. A culvert under the access road has overtopped, allowing sediment to be carried into the stream in this HQ watershed. As per a phone call with Joshua Martz from Diversified at 11:50 on April 2, equipment is expected to arrive on site in the morning of April 3. The visual cleanup of the site is expected to be completed at that time. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 855861
Permit API: 117-21688
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Delmar Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-07-16
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted a Follow-up inspection of the Seneca Resources - DCNR 007 Pad K located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 7/16/2019 @1300 hours. Activity onsite consisted of a front-end loader filling dump trucks with pad material that has been scraped up and stockpiled onsite. This material is being taken to DNCR 007 Pad D, to be used in the construction of the well pad. At the time of this inspection, the pad appears to have been scraped down, removing approximately 1.5' - 2' of pad material around the remaining secondary containment/rig mats. No puddles were observed onsite. Fluid in the gas buster secondary containment had a field measured conductivity of 4.23mS/cm. During a 5/21/19 inspection (IR#2885486) of the site, numerous puddles were discovered on the pad surface. Field screening indicated the conductivity ranged from 4 to >19.99 mS/cm. A sample was collected and upon the DEP receiving the results, they were communicated to Seneca and documented in an Administrative Inspection report (IR# 2897380) on 6/24/19. These results show elevated levels of chloride, strontium and barium indicating a release of a pollutional substance that exceeds Act 2 standards. This inspection report noted violations and requested information pertaining to the quantity of material released to the pad surface as well as what actions Seneca has done to remediate these releases. The NOV response received on 7/15/19 from Seneca failed to provide this information. Therefore, the violations cited will remain outstanding. Seneca should reference 78a66(c) to determine the actions necessary to achieve compliance at this location. I departed the site @1400 hours.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. All annuli were closed when I arrived w/ the exception of the 21HC (20x13) annulus and the 6H (9x5) annulus which were opened early.- Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Brendan Hollerand, Creston Consultant Reps., Shane Reimold and Alex Pashchuk. Starting at approx. 10:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Report Details

Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 920793
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/14/2021
Comments: On June 14, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline and Rob Marquez conducted a routine site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. The recently constructed access road and well pad has sparse vegetation growth occurring. The DEP recommends reseeding the site to prevent areas from eroding. An erosion rill has developed through the plunge pool on Culvert 7. The rill has washed sediment between two compost filter socks and off the LOD of the site. The DEP recommends adding and expanding stone to the downgrade side of the plunge pool to create a more gradual and level runoff and to slow the velocity of the flow. During the inspection, the plunge pool at culvert 9 was still being overwhelmed from the flow of water through the culvert. The DEP recommends excavating the sediment that has built up at the stacked filter socks. When the sediment has been excavated and the stacked filter socks have been dewatered, the DEP recommends removing the stacked filter socks. The filter sock that is located on the top of the plunge is recommended to be removed and to bring the level of stone up to the same level as the culvert outlet. At the time of inspection, the level of the plunge pool appears to be a foot lower than the culvert outlet. More stone is recommended to be added to create a more level overflow of the plunge pool which will slow the velocity of the water. The slope toe key drain outlet prior to Culvert No. 9 is flowing over the compost filter sock. The compost filter sock still appeared to be in place. The DEP recommends monitoring this area and replacing or repairing the compost filter sock as necessary. A seep has recently caused some erosion rills near the well pad entrance. The DEP recommends addressing the erosion rills and the seep. A channel has been dug to direct the seep towards the diversion berm. The sediment leaving the LOD at Culvert 7 is a violation of of Chapter 102.4(b)1 and Chapter 102.11(a)1.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/05/2026 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Findlay Township, Allegheny county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8260681
Permit API: 003-22553
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Findlay Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/05/2026
Comments: On January 5 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Ziolkowoski Well Site (NOT approved on 11/6/2023) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/4/2026 (CTS 394386). Present during the inspection was operator representative Nate Smiell.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel. The Department was unable to assess site stabilization due to snow coverage.At the time of inspection, there are 14 total wells on the well pad. According to Mr. Smiell, 8 of the wells (2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, 6H, 7H, 8H, and 9H) are completed/active wells. These wells were surrounded by protective barriers and appeared equipped for productions with well tags present. Mr. Smeill stated that stimulation for the other 6 wells (1H,10H,11H,12H,13H, and 14H) has been completed and they are currently in the process of drill outs for these wells.Upon inspection, all necessary drilling equipment appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No fluid leaks or spills were identified around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Smiell guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Smiell the release occurred on 1/4/2026. He stated the release was caused by 2 loose flange bolts on a 2-inch oil dump line located at the front of the #5 GPU. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of a produced water and condensate mixture released to the graveled well pad.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 4 foot radius around the #5 GPU. A background conductivity reading of 0.08mS was obtained. Conductivity readings of 2.76mS, 10.36mS, 2.14mS, and several readings of OR (Over Detectable Range, >20MS) were obtained in the area of the release. During the inspection, the Department observed active remediation of the spill occurring. Mr. Smiell stated that an air excavation/vacuum truck was being used to break up the ground and vacuum the contaminated material into waste containers. He stated that additional excavation by heavy machinery will occur as needed when the GPU is removed from its location as they plan to replace it upon competition of the active drill outs.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 6th post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on the 21HC, 22HC and the 23HC and the 1st PBUTs performed on the 5H and 6H since Perf. and Squeeze ops were completed on 5/16/22. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/12/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 978341
Permit API: 015-23678
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2022
Comments: Site inspection conducted as a follow up to Notice of Violations (NOV) associated inspection report #3373528 dated 6/6/2022 and administrative inspection report #3386649 dated 7/5/2022. There are no Blackhill Energy personnel on site at time of inspection. Weather conditions are overcast and 31 degrees F. During this inspection, completions equipment is still attached to the wells drilled and stimulated during 2021. Two sand separators and a 500 barrel gas buster tank appear to be connected to gas wells (photo 2). Puddled fluid on site was screened using an Oakton PCTS 50 water conductivity meter and a Hanna Groline soil conductivity meter. While screening puddles around the well heads and 500 barrel gas buster frac tank, the Department observed fluid draining from the tank and releasing onto secondary containment (photo 3). The containment is open along the north end discharge port and puddled fluid on containment appears to be flowing off containment into the pad surface (photo 4). Water within containment is observed with conductivity reading 'Over Range' (>19.99 mS/cm). Puddles screened outside of containment are observed to range between 9.8 mS/cm near the north well head to 'Over Range' in a puddle next to the tank secondary containment. Sample 4406-018 collected at 11:45 from fluid puddled on pad rock surface between tank secondary containment and north-most gas well (photo 7). Sample will be analyzed using SAC 942. The Department notified Regina Logue, Blackhill Energy Environmental Manager, that the tank was leaking at 12:15. Ms. Logue indicated that Blackhill personnel were en route to the site and that Moody's Environmental was contracted to conduct site characterization. Violation noted for potential pollution. Additional violations may be issued pending results of water sample analysis. Previous NOV's associated with inspection report #3373528 dated 6/6/2022 and administrative inspection report #3386649 dated 7/5/2022 remain outstanding.

Comments: On April 2, 2024, inspection conducted Brownlee Kelley 12333 well pad in Hopewell Township, Washington County. This inspection follows up to IR 3737318, which was conducted in response to a spill that occurred the day prior. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on August 6, 2021.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Heavy sedimentation was observed in the access road, with accelerated erosion rills observed in the access road closer to the well pad (see photos 2 and 3). However, the Department did not observe it entering off-site Waters of the Commonwealth. Flowback equipment and related secondary containment was removed from site, as well as the rolloff dumpsters containing the impacted material (see photo 4). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 5). All other machinery and primary containments that appear to contain regulated substances were placed within secondary containment. GPU units onsite were either placed within secondary containment or equipped with interconnected vertical separators (see photo 6). The area formerly impacted by the spill documented in IR 3737318 and IR 3736812 was freshly backfilled with no elevated conductivity detected (see photos 7-10). The ERP was onsite (see photo 10). Well 4H was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 13 and 14). There are eight other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 12).Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that the operator conduct immediate repairs to the access road in a manner that abates the aforementioned accelerated erosion and heavy sedimentation, and prevents it from worsening. Violations issued under IR 3737318 shall remain outstanding, as the NOI to Remediation of the release under Act 2 requirements have not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB Program. Additional violations are being issued against the accelerated erosion and heavy sedimentation observed in the access road.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Compliance Schedule Evaluation
Inspection Date: 8/19/2024
Comments: On August 19 2024,the Department (DEP) conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation inspection of the Nelson 2 OG Well in Dunbar Township, Fayette County. At the time of the inspection, the well appeared to be equipped for production.The well posting was present at the time of the inspection. The access road appeared to be stable with no signs of erosion or sedimentation issues. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the affected area of the pump jack fluid release documented in inspection reports 3552812 and 3728744. There were erosion and sedimentation issues at the well site and adjacent to the wellhead due to the prior releases of the fluid from the pump jack onto the ground in inspection reports 3552812 and 3728744. It appears the erosion that previously extended adjacent to and downslope from the well site is now exhibiting greater than 70% vegetative coverage with the exception of the area between the agricultural fence adjacent to the well site and the wellhead ;this area is located approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead. A background soil conductivity reading was taken. The soil conductivity reading was 0.0647mS. Soil conductivity readings were taken around the wellhead. The soil conductivity readings around the wellhead were 0.370mS, 1.341mS, and 0.1090mS. Soil conductivity readings around the wellhead with visually stained gravel were higher than the background reading. These readings indicate that the prior spills have not yet been remediated. It appears visually that the area around the wellhead and area extending approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead are not remediated due to the stained gravel,the lack of vegetation, and higher conductivity readings compared to the background reading. The area between the agricultural fence adjacent to the well site and the wellhead appear to still remain affected. This area is located approximately 10ft to 15ft from the wellhead had soil conductivity readings of 7.91mS, 6.65mS, and 5.16mS. Soil conductivity readings collected by the DEP today in the adjacent agricultural field that were affected in previous inspection report 3578365 dated June 22 2023 were 0.300mS, 0.158mS, 0.1114mS, 0.1059mS, 0.0840mS, 0.1342mS, 0.1586mS, 0.1711mS, and 0.0509mS. The Operator is currently under a Compliance ("Order) that was issued on August 9 2024.The Operator confirmed receipt of the Order via email on August 9 2024.In the Order were the following deadlines:Within 10 days from receipt of this Order, submit a site characterization plan to the Department. The site characterization plan should be developed to ensure uniform remediation of the Well Site. The plan should include a description and visual depiction of field screening and/or sampling locations and a narrative describing how contaminated material will be (or was completely) removed from locations exhibiting elevated conductivity and/or visibly impacted gravel and/or soils. Therefore, the due date for submission was 8/19/2024, a Site Characterization Plan has not been submitted to the DEP as of the time of this inspection. Within 10 days from receipt of this Order, submit receipts and/or other applicable documentation to the DEP to verify that the regulated substance(s) and contaminated soil was/were removed as described above and disposed of at a permitted facility. Receipts or documentation regarding the removal of contaminated soil or regulated substance(s) dated after the date of this Order shall be submitted to the DEP within 10 days of Apollo Resources receipt of such documentation. Therefore, the due date for submission was 8/19/2024, a Submission of receipts and/or other applicable documentation has not been submitted to the DEP as of the time of this inspt. Based on today's inspection, a violation shall remain outstanding for failure to comply with the Order. Unmet deadlines outlined in inspection report 3815768 remain unmet.

Violation ID: 922942

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/12/2021
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of JKLM's Headwaters 145 Pad located in Ulysses Township, Potter County on 7/12/2021 at 1040 hours. The weather was 76 degrees with mostly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a reported release of ~42 gallons of production fluid to the pad surface. The release occurred on Saturday, 7/10/2021, and was properly reported to the DEP. Complaint ID #357917 is tied to this release. On 7/10/2021, at approximately 1210 hours, a fitting on a hose line connected to a production line riser failed, causing a reported release of ~42 gallons of production fluid to the pad surface. A vacuum truck was onsite when the release occurred and was able to vacuum up the fluid that was visible. Excavation of the pad material began on Saturday. A rain event on Sunday evening caused pooling of water in the excavated areas, which was again vacuumed up. Environmental consultant, Whipper Hill was onsite during the inspection on Monday, where screening and excavating of the impacted area was being conducted. Whipper Hill reported elevated soil conductivity readings from 3-6mS/cm. I screened the impacted area for soil conductivity with a Hanna Groline soil tester. Some isolated areas were field measured >4.00mS/cm. Standing water along the edge of the pad closest to the release was field measured at ~370us/cm today (see photo #5). The release was contained to the pad surface and no erosion & sediment controls or stormwater controls were affected. The impacted area was still being screened and excavated when I left the site. Based on the findings outlined within this inspection report, violations of the following are cited against API # 105-21875 at this time: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301 Due to the volume of the release being reported at ~42 gallons and then a commingling of impacted soils and rainwater after the initial release, this release will be referred to the DEP's Cleanups and Brownfields Program for attainment with Act 2 standards. I departed the site at 1150 hours.

The previously observed excavated material covered with plastic liners appeared to be removed from the site. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/04/2023
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 981057
Permit API: 125-28981
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Buffalo Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/04/2023
Comments: On January 4, 2023, the Department responded to a spill reported by the Operator at the DMC Properties East Unit in Buffalo Township, Washington County. PPC Plan was on site.According to Range Resources, the incident occurred on 1/4/2023 at appx. 10:10 and was reported to the Department on the same date at appx. 11:50. The discharge was caused by a contracted company that failed to place a cam-lock cap on the 4" port on the back of the vacuum box, resulting in the discharge of an estimated 20 gallons of flow back water as the box was loaded onto the truck. The spill was contained within the well pad and in Photos 1-4 the estimated spill area can be seen as outlined in orange. Utilizing a vacuum truck, one vacuum box (Photo 5) was being filled with impacted gravel and all waste at the time of this inspection. Range Resources intends to remediate this release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1) and informed the Department that disposal documents will be sent to the Department as part of a closure summary. Range Resources estimates that the impacted material will be removed by tomorrow 1/5/2023.
